_about: Snap's orchard (docs/modes/snap-design.md D5, D9.2): a Snap-owned sidecar scene, greybox. Nani's fruit trees as a still picture 1.5-2 screens wide (world units on the 1600x900 design; this file is the full 2-screen width and a level uses the first `sceneWidth` screens). Fruit hang in clusters on branch bands. The clusters themselves are data (the `patterns` below), but WHICH fruit hangs WHERE is dealt per round from the seed (js/snap/requests.js layout), so a round's scene can't be learnt from the last one (design 10, loop 3: scene memory). Every spot the layout makes carries {id, kind, size, x, y, w, h, layer: 'branch'}. Size classes are the fruit's true size, never its size on screen. The fruit are the game's existing item sprites (assets/items/fruit/<id>.png) drawn into their box; the evaluator (js/snap/photo.js) only ever sees the boxes. The frame always sits in the middle of the stage, so no fruit is ever under the prints tray (no tray_safe band is needed for a still scene).
name: Nani's orchard

bands._about: Branch bands (the y of each row of clusters). Count clusters are two fruit tall, so two bands; size clusters are one row, so three.

patterns._about: Offsets in units of `spacing` [x, y] from the cluster's centre. A count cluster holds one to six fruit of one kind (two kinds when a level interleaves); a size cluster is one kind in three clear sizes, spaced wider so each can be the main subject on its own.

photobomber._about: Level 3: a bunch of another kind hung close beside a cluster, on either side, so leaving it out ('nar kelo') is a framing choice.
